title: Official plan boundary, debt issue and levels of service
subtitle: Community grants, minister's zoning orders, hospital update, wastewater bypass questions and county report on transfer station closure
overview: Council endorsed staff comments on County of Wellington Official Plan Amendment 126, which sets the new urban boundaries for Fergus and Elora. The county adjusted the boundary to avoid splitting farm parcels. Staff support those changes and asked for further tweaks, including adding one small parcel near Elora. The vote was {{vote:m4}}.

Council directed staff to work with Toronto Dominion Bank on a debt issue of up to $27.7 million, using a fixed rate borrowing with an interest rate swap. It also endorsed a levels of service framework that will feed the 2025 asset management plan update, due under provincial rules by July 1. Community Investment Fund grants were approved, including extra support for two long-standing local festivals and agricultural events.

Council received a staff report explaining minister's zoning orders and approved routine consent items, including wastewater plant reports and Business Improvement Area board appointments. A hospital update and a county report were also presented. The county report said the Elora transfer station closes after April 5 for renovations.

decisions.detail: Council endorsed the staff report and authorized the Managing Director of Planning and Development to send its comments on the amendment to the County of Wellington {{vote:m4}}.
Council directed staff to work with Toronto Dominion Bank on a fixed rate borrowing with an interest rate swap of up to $27.7 million for 2025 long-term borrowing needs {{vote:m6}}.
Council endorsed the draft levels of service framework and directed staff to use it to draft the 2025 asset management plan update {{vote:m3}}.

Council approved the grant allocations recommended by the Healthy Communities Advisory Committee, including one-time support for the Fergus Agricultural Society and Fergus Scottish Festival {{vote:m2}}.
Council approved the consent items, including Business Improvement Area board appointments for Fergus and Elora and receipt of 2024 wastewater and treasurer reports {{vote:m1}}.
Council received for information a staff report responding to a housing delegation, explaining how minister's zoning orders work {{vote:m5}}.

debate: On OPA 126, one councillor objected to part of the county's red boundary near South Fergus. Staff replied that the change reduces agricultural impact by avoiding split parcels and has no bearing on the separate battery storage application.
Councillors asked whether the proposed Elora parcel should be joined by the rest of its surrounding block. Staff agreed this made sense and said the county could be asked to consider it.

On minister's zoning orders, one councillor suggested the report state that the township stays open to the tool. Others said that wording would be too specific, and that applications should be handled as they arise and local planning is best done locally.

On the debt issue, a councillor asked about risk if provincial development charges were cut or removed, since most of the debt would be repaid from them. Staff said they could slow some projects, reserves are stable, and internal debt limits are well below the provincial cap.

On wastewater, a councillor asked about 2024 bypasses at the Fergus plant. Staff said they involved sand filter mechanical problems, effluent stayed within limits, repairs were made, and a master plan review may consider upgrades.
